units.text: INT. FERRY TERMINAL LAUNDROMAT - NIGHT
A concrete room beside the ticket hall.
Twelve washers, eight dryers, a vending machine for soap.
Fluorescent tubes buzz.
Through a salt-stained window, the last ferry sits at its slip like a lit apartment block.
NADIRA HAQ, 30, in a rain jacket, hair braided back, holds a basket against her hip.
She is staring at Dryer Six.
In Dryer Six, a pair of red socks goes around and around.
On a plastic bench near the door sits ELLIS "BIRDIE" PAYNE, 28, Nadira's younger sister, in a big sweater, headphones around her neck.
She watches Nadira like someone watching a pot.
At the folding table stands GUS TREMBLAY, 33, a sailor off a freighter in a navy peacoat, folding a single white shirt into thirds.
He has a duffel at his feet.
He does not know the sisters.
He knows only that they are loud in the quiet way.
At the counter, behind sliding glass, MR. FITCH, 70s, the attendant, reads a newspaper he has read before.
You're staring at them.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: I'm not.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: Nadi. They're his socks.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: They're not his. They're mine. They just look like his.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: You bought red socks after he left.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: Not because of him.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: Because of the color red?
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: Nadira finally turns.
She sets the basket on the table next to Gus, who slides his shirt to the side without comment.
She starts pulling out towels, aggressively.
I said I'd be fine, and I am.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: You flooded the bathroom.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: That was the tap.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: You were holding a mug at the time.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: Gus coughs, politely.
Nadira glances at him, then back at her sister.
Can we do this at home?
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: We're not at home. We're at the ferry terminal because you wouldn't let me drive you.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: I wanted to be on the water.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: You wanted to be on the water and instead you're in a laundromat.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: Nadira stops.
She holds a towel in both hands.
The ferry horn sounds outside, one long note.
Mr. Fitch turns a page.
He said he'd be on that one.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: Birdie stands.
Takes off her headphones.
Walks over, slow, like approaching a horse.
Nadi.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: He said Thursday. The ten forty. He said, "I'll see you on the ten forty."
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: Okay.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: And I thought, if I'm already here, I'll just see him get off. And then I can decide.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: Decide what?
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: If I'm angry!
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: It rings in the little room.
Gus becomes interested in a button.
Mr. Fitch lowers the paper by an inch.
I don't know what I am.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: You're soggy, mostly.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: Nadira makes a noise that is half laugh and half something else.
She drops the towel onto the table and presses the heels of her hands to her eyes.
Birdie puts both arms around her from behind.
The red socks go around and around.
Excuse me. Ma'am.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Both sisters turn.
The ten forty is cancelled. Engine trouble. They told us on the dock.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Cancelled?
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: The next one's seven in the morning.
units.name: GUS

units.text: So he's not on it.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: I don't know who "he" is. But nobody's on it.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Silence.
Nadira looks at Birdie.
Birdie looks at Nadira.
Then Nadira begins to laugh, properly, helplessly, and sits down on the bench with her hand over her mouth, shoulders shaking.
Birdie sits next to her.
Oh my God.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: He's not even coming.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: Nobody's coming, Nadi.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: I could have stayed home!
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: You could have stayed home.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: They lean into each other, laughing, wiping their eyes.
Gus returns to his shirt, folds the last third, and tucks it into the duffel.
A small smile.
Dryer Six is done, by the way.
units.name: MR. FITCH

units.text: Thanks, Mr. Fitch.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: Take the socks out. They'll shrink.
units.name: MR. FITCH

units.text: She stands.
Crosses to Dryer Six.
Opens the door and the warm air rolls out over her face.
She takes out the red socks, holds them up, looks at them for a long moment.
They're just socks.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: They're great socks.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: They are great socks.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: Nadira pairs them.
Slips them into her basket.
Birdie slings her headphones back around her neck.
Gus lifts his duffel.
Good luck, ladies.
units.name: GUS

units.text: You too, sailor.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: He nods at them, at Mr. Fitch, and goes out into the wind.
The door sighs shut.
Nadira lifts the basket, and Birdie takes the other handle without being asked.
Seven in the morning.
units.name: NADIRA

units.text: I'll make you eggs first.
units.name: BIRDIE

units.text: They carry the basket out together.
Mr. Fitch watches them go, then turns the page.
